$note: Golden fixture for canonicalisation and the corpus digest (E-014).
WHAT IT IS FOR. `canonicalize` decides what a checksum MEANS. Change it and every digest
ever recorded becomes wrong — in these files, in the version ledger, and later in Postgres
— with no import edge to the data and no test that would notice, because both sides of
every comparison would move together. With zero authored entries there is nothing else in
the repository that could catch it. This fixture is that check.
HOW THE EXPECTED VALUES WERE PRODUCED. Each `sha256` is `createHash('sha256')` from
node:crypto over the UTF-8 bytes of the `canonical` string EXACTLY as written here. They
were NOT produced by running this package's code over the `input` — that would compare the
implementation to itself and go green for free. The test asserts two separate things:
THE HASHER ITSELF is checked against the published SHA-256 vectors in src/digest.ts
(SHA256_VECTORS), so a hasher that is not SHA-256 fails before it reaches these rows.
CHANGING A VALUE HERE is changing what a corpus checksum means and requires an ADR.

cases.name: empty-object
cases.note: The degenerate case. If this moves, the serialiser changed shape entirely.

cases.name: empty-array
cases.note: Distinct from the empty object, and must hash differently.

cases.name: keys-sorted
cases.note: Written out of order on purpose: the canonical form must be b-after-a regardless.

cases.name: kanji-and-kana
cases.note: Non-ASCII stays as characters, never \u escapes, and the hash is over UTF-8 bytes. A serialiser that escaped them, or a hasher that encoded UTF-16, changes this row.

cases.name: tristimulus-triple
cases.note: Array order is data and is preserved. Number formatting is shortest round-trip.

cases.name: explicit-null
cases.note: FR-21 makes null a value with meaning, so it must be serialised and hashed, not skipped.

cases.name: fractional-weight
cases.note: 0.9 is not exactly representable in binary64; the canonical form is the shortest string that round-trips to the same double.
